text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Finnish telecom equipment group Nokia and its Swedish rival Ericsson say they support Japanese proposal to develop wide-band CDMA, a third-generation mobile phone standard.
- Three of the planned euro coins will be made of a 'Golden Nordic' metal mixture produced by Finnish metals and mining group Outokumpu. @
- Forest fires have devastated hundreds of hectares of land in various parts in Finland.
- Justice and interior ministries considering banning motorcycle gangs after wave of gang violence in Nordic region.
- Finnish lottery winners avoid bragging and ostentatious living, a study shows.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Wealthy Finnish Paper Workers' Union wants buffer funds against economic fluctuations in European economic and monetary union, EMU. @
- Finnish forestry group Enso plans to invest 540 million markka at its German Hotlzmann paper mills.
- Fourteen Finnish companies were ranked among the top 1,000 major global companies in a listing by Industry Week.
AAMULEHTI

- European forestries should be capable of industrial investment and environmental protection, said Ian Hunter, director of the European Forest Institute on a visit to Finland, but added that forest certification will hardly ever cover all forests in Europe. @
- Finland will host Nordic peace-keeping manoeuvres in 1999, Defence Minister Anneli Taina says.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finland's price level is still higher than that of other OECD countries; only Denmark and Sweden among EU members are more expensive, OECD figures show.
- Jarmo Lahteenmaki, the leader of the Finnish Paper Workers' Union, was re-elected to a second four-year term.
- Finland is ready to sell weapons to Estonia, Defence Minister Anneli Taina says. @
- The special position of Finland's Aland Islands is secure, President Martti Ahtisaari said on Monday at the festivities for the 75th anniversary of the islands' provincial autonomy.
- The Finnish health sector has sprouted many techologically innovative small firms in recent years.
DEMARI
- Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions SAK will support the paper workers union's efforts to solve its branch-related problems, SAK leader Lauri Ihalainen says.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
